text:
Maya: Heads-up — ran an 8-node TP stress job on prod cluster and hit repeated timeouts during step 362. Several ranks timed out at rendezvous, appears to be all-reduce waiting for a straggler. Can people triage?

Leo: Saw this too on a couple of Canary runs earlier. Noticed tail latency spike right after the batching heuristic change we shipped yesterday. Might be batching + kernel routing mismatch.

Jun: Can you paste the rendezvous trace? Also which kernel selector commit rolled?

Maya: Pasting the condensed log excerpt: ```RANK 3: waiting at ALLREDUCE barrier for 12.4s; last recv from RANK 7 at 12.4s before timeout
RANK 7: completed local forward but stalled on kernel launch (cuLaunchKernel err=0x700)
-- kvcache stats: hit_rate=0.89 evictions=0 in last 10s
-- batching window: avg_microbatch=2, dynamic_batching_enabled=true```

Ashley: Quick note: the kernel-selector change (rev b3f2) added an afallback path that prefers smaller kernel blocks for short sequences. It also changed the runtime to favor packing more microbatches before launching to improve throughput. Could increase overlap but might induce head-of-line issues on some shapes.

Leo: That matches. If microbatch packing delays kernel launch, the all-reduce bandwidth schedule can be skewed across ranks and cause rendezvous desync. We saw similar pattern in earlier experiments but only on single-node. Multi-node networking latency amplifies it.

perf-ci: Perf test summary (latest): "tp-scaling-8node": median step=210ms -> 225ms, p99=1.8s -> 6.2s after change; allreduce-wait-time p99 increased from 140ms -> 4.1s.

Jun: Repro plan: 1) force kernel-selector to previous release (rollback b3f2) on canary pool; 2) run small microbatch stress with forced kvcache disabled to isolate caching; 3) capture nvprof + NCCL traces.

Maya: Rolling rollback to previous kernel-selector on two canaries now. Also toggled dynamic_batching=false for the run.

deploy-bot: Rollback initiated by Maya. Targets: canary-1, canary-2. ETA ~4m.

Ashley: If rollback fixes it we should separate the two features (kernel fallback vs packing) in the selector change so we can re-enable safer part. Also add a guard that prevents increased packing if inter-node RTT > threshold.

Leo: While we wait, attaching a small nccl timeline snippet I pulled from the failed run: ```TIMELINE: RANK0 send->start 0.0ms; RANK1 delayed start 3150ms; RANK3 waiting->start 12400ms; congestion window stable but missing launch sync on ranks 1/3/7```

Maya: Canary rollback completed. First run after rollback: step median 208ms, p99 230ms, no rendezvous timeouts in 30 runs. Looks promising.

Jun: Good. Action items: - Revert packing change in kernel-selector and land as two separate PRs. - Add a perf test that simulates inter-node skew with variable microbatch packing. - Add a kvcache diagnostic flag to emit per-rank prelaunch timing to help spot launch skew earlier.

Ashley: I'll open the PR to split the selector change. Also will add an opt-in runtime flag `--disable-packing` for staging.

Maya: Thanks — follow-up doc in #eng-runtime with traces + perf numbers. Putting incident as Sev3 since rollback resolved. :thumbsup:

Leo: One more note: we should consider kernel affinity pinning for critical kernels to reduce variability from CUDNN heuristics across nodes. Added to backlog.

Maya: Closing thread; leave comments if you find regressions on other jobs.
